A group of 21 news publishers has challenged the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 , India’s privacy law, in court, arguing it would trample investigative work and let the government identify journalists’ sources, documents show.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government announced the implementation of the law in 2025 to protect the digital personal data of ⁠users, raising compliance requirements for platforms like Meta and Google. The publishers have said that since media outlets were not exempt, the law was an invasion of press freedom.

Media companies received assurances in an August meeting with the government that the law would protect press freedom, but not having a written carve-out for journalists like in the European Union, Singapore and Britain was alarming, the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) said in a confidential filing at the Supreme Court, reviewed by Reuters .

The October 6, 2026 lawsuit, being reported for the first time and due to be heard on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), is the most high-profile challenge to the government’s privacy law. ⁠Until now, only free speech activists and a group of smaller news outlets had challenged it.

The costs of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption fall unevenly across workers, with entry-level jobs particularly at risk, according to a whitepaper by the Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI) at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT-Madras).

“The entry-level career pipeline is especially at risk,” the paper says, highlighting differences in how AI affects entry-level and experienced workers, formal and informal workers, urban and rural workers, and employees in micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and large firms.

Titled ‘How AI Is Reconfiguring Work in India: A Task-Based Framework for Understanding Augmentation, Displacement, New Roles and the Changing Structure of Jobs’, the paper examines how AI automates tasks within jobs and how this can lead to changes in work, new roles or displacement.

The paper identifies differences in firms’ ability to adopt AI. Large companies can absorb the fixed costs of integrating and customising advanced models, while MSMEs depend more on narrow, subsidised tools. It also flags differences between English and regional-language work, noting that Indian-language AI performs less well on nuanced, code-switched conversations.

Automation is also creating new roles, including robot operators and AI escalation specialists. However, the paper says its evidence does not systematically track whether such roles offer stable employment or piecework, a distinction that affects how much of the productivity gains reaches workers.

The paper says its framework is “largely silent” on changes in job quality because Indian evidence is limited. It identifies wages, workplace monitoring, work intensity, stress and burnout, career progression, the quality of human interaction and responsibility for errors as areas requiring further study.

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday (October 23, 2026) that he would speak to tech tycoon Elon Musk if there are still problems with Ukraine's military-grade version of the Starlink service.

A possible merger between Elon Musk ’s rocket company SpaceX and carmaker Tesla may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between US President Donald Trump and the Democrats.

Musk revived speculation about a tie-up this week, calling a combination “a good idea” and confirming that committees at both companies were reviewing a potential deal, a step toward what could become the largest merger in history ⁠and create a company worth about $3.5 trillion.

But a merger would also unite one of the US government’s most important aerospace and defense contractors with one of the most China-exposed major American manufacturers — a combination likely to raise questions about national security risks both in Washington and in Beijing.

Those concerns are unlikely to derail a deal, analysts said, but they would likely leave the combined company exposed to years of political wrangling and pressure from both sides of the Pacific.

Tesla’s China operations, they said, could become a source of leverage for Beijing in any future dispute with Washington, while a Democratic takeover of the US House of Representatives in next month’s midterm elections could subject the deal to congressional investigations and political ⁠maneuvering.

Democrats immediately raised concerns about the deal’s implications, signaling their intent to turn the merger into a political flashpoint ahead ⁠of the November 3 midterms.

headline: India’s smartphone shipments collapsed to a decade low during Q3 2026
body: During Q3, 2026, Samsung became the top smartphone brand in India, followed by Vivo and Oppo
full_body:

India’s smartphone shipments fell to a decade low by 20% year-over-year (YoY) during Q3 2026, noted Counterpoint Research. This steep fall during the July-September period was mainly due to high memory prices that led to constant increase in smartphone costs which resulted in softer demand, as OEMs held inventories.

“Rising component costs pushed device prices higher, putting increasing pressure on affordability and weakening the traditional mass-market volume engine, particularly below ₹15,000,” said Research Analyst Shubham Singh. “Sub-₹20,000 shipments declined by 47% in Q3 2026 as rising model prices pushed devices into higher price bands,” he added.

During Q3, 2026, Samsung became the top smartphone brand in India, after nine quarters, with a 17% share. The Galaxy A series drove volumes, the research firm said.

Vivo came second with a 16% share as their Y series continued to drive volumes. Oppo was at third position with a 12% market share. Xiaomi ranked fourth with a 12% share.

Counterpoint said that Apple iPhone 18 Pro series seen a strong start in India, with initial sales nearly 20% higher YoY than those of the iPhone 17 Pro series. It also mentioned that there’s a continued demand for the iPhone 17 lineup even after Apple pricing adjustments across its portfolio.

MediaTek was the top chipset OEM with a 45% share in Q3 2026 in India.
